captured_note: Ported from the capture's self-contained methods/25_mae, whose models/mae_vit.py is the lab's OWN MAE implementation ('own implementation', following He et al. 2021), torch-only and trained from scratch. It is not a copy of the CC-BY-NC facebookresearch/mae code and uses no pretrained weights, so MAE ports self-contained -- the treatment the other re-implemented methods received -- with no third_party submodule. (The inventory's ARSSL/third_party/mae, CC-BY-NC, is a different artifact and is not used here.)

paper.title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners
paper.authors: He, Chen, Xie, Li, Dollar, Girshick

encoder: encoder.pt is the encoder side of the model: the patch embedding (patch_embed), the CLS token, the encoder blocks (enc_blocks) and their norm (enc_norm). The decoder (dec_embed, dec_blocks, dec_norm, dec_pred, mask_token) is reconstruction machinery and is excluded. The sin-cos enc_pos_embed is a non-persistent buffer, recomputed deterministically on build, so it is not stored.
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the MAE encoder's global-average-pooled patch features (He et al. Section 4), a genuine learned representation -- so the number is comparable. Follows the lab's ARSSL probe (L2-normalise + mean-centre, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5).
rewritten_during_the_port: the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA (the lab wrapper reached CUDA through init_distributed_mode)
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch)
the training loop drops the upstream DistributedDataParallel and the TensorBoard logging so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged
DATA_ROOT is the dataset root; the pretrain stage reads its train/ subdirectory (unified data-root convention via adapterlib.dataset_split_dir).
